title: One job, done more than once
idea: MEET: notice when the SAME sub-job appears several times in a task. No code.

exercises.prompt: TASK: 'Print a welcome banner at the top, and the SAME banner at the bottom.' What do you notice?
options: The same job (print the banner) happens twice
The banner is only printed once
exercises.explanation: The banner job appears twice. A repeated job is a strong hint you've found a reusable sub-plan.

exercises.prompt: If the same little job shows up several times in a task, that job is a good candidate to name and reuse.
exercises.explanation: Exactly. A job you do again and again is worth naming once, so you don't rewrite it each time.

exercises.prompt: TASK: 'Show the header, show the report, show the header again.' How many TIMES does the header job run?
exercises.explanation: 'Show the header' appears at the start and the end - twice. The report job happens once in between.

exercises.prompt: Which of these tasks contain a REPEATED sub-job? (Pick all.)
options: Print a line of stars, then text, then a line of stars
Say hello to player 1, then say hello to player 2
exercises.explanation: The stars job repeats, and the 'say hello' job repeats for each player. The other two have no repeat.

exercises.prompt: Doing the exact same steps again by RE-TYPING them each time has a downside. What is it?
options: If the steps need a change, you must fix every copy
exercises.explanation: Copies drift and break. Fixing one copy but not the others is a classic bug. Reuse avoids that.

exercises.prompt: What's a better idea than copying the same steps three times?
options: Name the job once and use that name three times
exercises.explanation: Name it once, reuse the name. One place to read, one place to fix. That's what sub-plans are for.

exercises.prompt: Match each task to its repeated sub-job.

pairs.left: draw a line between each section

exercises.explanation: In each task, one small job is reused several times. That job is the natural sub-plan.

exercises.prompt: Reusing a named job keeps the main plan short and easy to read.
exercises.explanation: Yes. The main plan just says the job's name instead of repeating all its steps. Shorter and clearer.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: a different way to repeat work is a loop. When is a loop the better fit?
options: When you repeat the SAME steps for each item in a sequence
When each repeat is a totally different job
exercises.explanation: Loops repeat steps over items. A named sub-plan is for a job you call by name at chosen moments - sometimes both help.

options: spot a job that repeats, so it can be named once and reused
exercises.explanation: Seeing the repeat is the clue. Next, you'll learn to name that job - and then to write it as real code.
